source.subject: Biology
source.unit: Unit 1 — Diversity in the Living World
source.source_scope: Only the content printed on PDF page 12 (printed page 21): the end of plant virus symptoms, Viroids, Prions, Lichens, and the first part of the chapter Summary.

questions.question: Which symptoms of viral infection in plants are mentioned at the top of this page?
questions.explanation: The page continues the list of plant virus symptoms with vein clearing, dwarfing and stunted growth.
questions.source_text: and vein clearing, dwarfing and stunted growth.

questions.question: Viroids were discovered in 1971 by:
questions.explanation: The page credits T.O. Diener with discovering viroids in 1971.
questions.source_text: Viroids : In 1971, T.O. Diener discovered a new infectious agent that was smaller than viruses

questions.question: Viroids caused which disease when discovered?
questions.explanation: The page says the agent discovered by Diener caused potato spindle tuber disease.
questions.source_text: caused potato spindle tuber disease.

questions.question: How do viroids differ from viruses?
options: They consist of abnormally folded protein
They have both DNA and RNA
They are free RNA lacking the protein coat found in viruses
They have a protein coat but no nucleic acid
questions.explanation: The page says the viroid was a free RNA that lacked the protein coat found in viruses, hence its name.
questions.source_text: It was found to be a free RNA; it lacked the protein coat that is found in viruses, hence the name viroid.

questions.question: The RNA of the viroid was of:
questions.explanation: The page says the RNA of the viroid was of low molecular weight.
questions.source_text: The RNA of the viroid was of low molecular weight.

questions.question: Prions are infectious agents that consist of:
questions.explanation: The page says certain infectious neurological diseases are transmitted by an agent consisting of abnormally folded protein, called prions.
questions.source_text: transmitted by an agent consisting of abnormally folded protein.

questions.question: Which disease caused by prions is commonly called mad cow disease?
questions.explanation: The page says BSE is commonly called mad cow disease in cattle, and its analogous variant in humans is CJD.
questions.source_text: bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) commonly called mad cow disease in cattle

questions.question: The human disease analogous to BSE, caused by prions, is:
questions.explanation: The page names Creutzfeldt-Jacob disease (CJD) as the analogous variant in humans.
questions.source_text: its analogous variant Creutzfeldt–Jacob disease (CJD) in humans.

questions.question: Match each with its description from this page.
column_b: B. Symbiotic association of algae and fungi
C. Free RNA lacking a protein coat
questions.explanation: Viroids are free RNA without a protein coat, prions are abnormally folded proteins, and lichens are algae-fungus symbioses.
questions.source_text: It was found to be a free RNA ... an agent consisting of abnormally folded protein ... Lichens are symbiotic associations i.e. mutually useful associations, between algae and fungi.

questions.question: Lichens are symbiotic associations between:
questions.explanation: The page defines lichens as mutually useful associations between algae and fungi.
questions.source_text: Lichens are symbiotic associations i.e. mutually useful associations, between algae and fungi.

questions.question: Match each lichen component with its name and nutritional mode.
questions.explanation: The algal component is the phycobiont (autotrophic) and the fungal component is the mycobiont (heterotrophic).
questions.source_text: The algal component is known as phycobiont and fungal component as mycobiont, which are autotrophic and heterotrophic, respectively.

questions.question: In a lichen, which partner prepares food, and which provides shelter and absorbs mineral nutrients and water?
options: Fungi prepare food; algae provide shelter
Algae prepare food; fungi provide shelter and absorb minerals and water
Algae absorb minerals; fungi prepare food
questions.explanation: The page says algae prepare food for fungi, and fungi provide shelter and absorb mineral nutrients and water for the partner.
questions.source_text: Algae prepare food for fungi and fungi provide shelter and absorb mineral nutrients and water for its partner.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Lichens are very good pollution indicators.
Reason (R): Lichens do not grow in polluted areas.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation: The page gives the absence of lichens in polluted areas as the basis for their use as pollution indicators.
questions.source_text: are very good pollution indicators – they do not grow in polluted areas.

questions.question: According to the summary, who first proposed biological classification of plants and animals on the basis of simple morphological characters?
questions.explanation: The summary says classification was first proposed by Aristotle based on simple morphological characters.
questions.source_text: Biological classification of plants and animals was first proposed by Aristotle on the basis of simple morphological characters.

questions.question: According to the summary, Linnaeus later classified all living organisms into how many kingdoms?
questions.explanation: The summary says Linnaeus classified all living organisms into two kingdoms, Plantae and Animalia.
questions.source_text: Linnaeus later classified all living organisms into two kingdoms – Plantae and Animalia.

questions.question: Which of the following were the main criteria of the five kingdom classification listed in the summary?
questions.explanation: The summary lists cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition and reproduction, and phylogenetic relationships.
questions.source_text: The main criteria of the five kingdom classification were cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition and reproduction, and phylogenetic relationships.

questions.question: Which are the four classes of Kingdom Fungi listed in the summary?
questions.explanation: The summary names Phycomycetes, Ascomycetes, Basidiomycetes and Deuteromycetes. Chrysophytes and Dinoflagellates are Protista.
questions.source_text: Phycomycetes, Ascomycetes, Basidiomycetes and Deuteromycetes are the four classes under this kingdom.

questions.question: According to the summary, Kingdom Protista includes single-celled eukaryotes such as:
questions.explanation: The summary lists Chrysophytes, Dinoflagellates, Euglenoids, Slime-moulds and Protozoans.
questions.source_text: Kingdom Protista includes all single-celled eukaryotes such as Chrysophytes, Dinoflagellates, Euglenoids, Slime-moulds and Protozoans.

questions.question: According to the summary, the mode of nutrition of most fungi is:
questions.explanation: The summary says most fungi are saprophytic in their mode of nutrition.
questions.source_text: Most fungi are saprophytic in their mode of nutrition.

questions.question: According to the summary, the life cycle of plants exhibits:
options: Alternation of generations – gametophytic and sporophytic
questions.explanation: The summary says plant life cycles exhibit alternation of generations between gametophytic and sporophytic generations.
questions.source_text: The life cycle of plants exhibit alternation of generations – gametophytic and sporophytic generations.
